questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why money demand falls in hyperinflation
questions.stem: In a nurse's handover, Nurse Ada notes that during hyperinflation patients spend wages immediately because holding cash loses value fast, so money demand

options.text: falls because the opportunity cost of holding money soars
stays unchanged because nominal income still equals spending
options.misconception: ignores the erosion of real balances

options.text: rises as people hoard cash to hedge against rising prices
options.misconception: confuses money demand with hoarding behavior

options.text: rises because velocity of money decreases sharply

questions.explanation: Hyperinflation raises the cost of holding money, so real balances shrink and money demand falls. The tempting idea that people hoard cash ignores the inflation tax on balances.
questions.hint: Think about the cost of holding cash when prices explode.

questions.explanation: Subtract inflation from the nominal rate to get the real rate: 8 minus 3 equals 5 percent. Using addition or ignoring inflation gives the wrong real return.

options.text: the price level rises by about 10 percent

options.misconception: assumes money growth raises real output

questions.explanation: With stable velocity and output, money growth maps one-for-one to price growth. The tempting output-absorption idea ignores the long-run neutrality of money.
questions.hint: Hold velocity and output constant in MV=PY.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Nurse Grace's handover asks why velocity of money shoots up in a hyperinflation episode

answer.exemplar: Velocity rises because people rush to spend cash before it loses value, so money changes hands far more often and the same stock of money supports a much larger nominal flow of spending.

questions.explanation: When prices explode, holding money is costly, so agents spend quickly and velocity surges. The mistaken view that velocity falls confuses money demand with money supply.

questions.explanation: Persistent money creation to fund deficits drives hyperinflation. The harmless-liquidity view ignores that excess money chases limited goods and raises prices.
